description: Benjamin Netanyahu visits a military outpost in Gaza and insists Israel will not withdraw from occupied areas.
Donald Trump brokers a ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas in Gaza.
An independent UN inquiry publishes findings that Israel continued to commit genocide by deliberately targeting Palestinian children in Gaza.
Israel holds national elections, in which Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party is polling to gain about seven seats.
William III of Orange invaded England with 500 ships and 20,000 soldiers, forcing King James II to flee into exile in France.
JNIM and the Tuareg-dominated FLA launch a joint offensive in Mali against strategic towns and government and Russian forces.
A suicide attack in Kati, Mali, kills the Malian defence minister at his residence.
Rebels seize the strategic city of Kidal in Mali after soldiers and Russian mercenaries flee or surrender.
Al-Qaida launches the 9/11 attacks against targets in Washington and New York.
The US kills Ayman al-Zawahiri in Kabul.
The US carries out airstrikes in Nigeria against Islamic State-linked militant groups.
The Global Peace Index publishes its 2026 report noting Sahel terrorism death tolls.
Voters in Saxony-Anhalt hand the far-right AfD a resounding election win over Merz's CDU in the state election.
Merz and AfD co-leader Alice Weidel clash in a Bundestag debate, where Weidel pledges that the CDU will never win another election.
Voters in Berlin go to the polls in a state election where the CDU is expected to lose ground.
Voters in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania go to the polls in a state election where the CDU is expected to lose ground.
Merz convenes a meeting of the CDU leadership in Berlin to coordinate a response to the state election results.
Merz takes office as German chancellor, promising to cut back the AfD.
Russia holds parliamentary elections in which the ruling United Russia party wins a record 355 seats in the Duma.
Russia's supreme court bans the anti-war Yabloko party from participating in the elections.
Chechnya's leader Ramzan Kadyrov is re-elected with more than 99% of the votes.
Ukraine strikes Moscow's oil refinery as part of its deep strikes.
Russia carries out an overnight attack on the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, damaging a residential building, a university building, a shopping centre and a boiler house.
Ukrainian forces capture two North Korean prisoners of war in Russia's Kursk region.
Zelenskyy and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung agree to resolve the prisoner of war issue while respecting the soldiers' free will.
Zelenskyy tells the UN General Assembly that Ukraine sent two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea.
The two North Korean prisoners of war reportedly arrive in South Korea via a third country.
South Korea summons Ukraine's chargé d'affaires in Seoul and demands an apology at governmental level.
Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
South Korea pledges a $100m support package for Ukraine.
Iran's military attacks the Ahmad al-Jaber air base in Kuwait, used by US forces, with missiles and drones.
Iran's military attacks the Al Minhad air base in the UAE, used by US forces, with missiles and drones.
Kuwait's air defences intercept Iranian missile and drone attacks.
Bahrain and Jordan's air defence systems intercept several Iranian air attacks.
The US strikes Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Antarctic winter sea ice peaks at 17.59 million square kilometres, about a million square kilometres below the average maximum.
A heatwave with temperatures 20C above normal hits the Antarctic peninsula.
A large area of the Amundsen Sea loses sea ice in early August.
Typhoon Saudel brings days of torrential rain to Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces in south-east China.
Authorities in Fujian evacuate almost 600,000 people from high-risk, flood-prone areas.
More than 2,500 teachers and students are trapped in a school compound in Wenzhou, Zhejiang, after flash floods.
A river embankment collapses in Putian, Fujian, flattening 100 homes and requiring at least 1,260 people to be rescued.
A landslip in a village of Suichuan county, Jiangxi, kills three people and leaves nine missing.
The South African Weather Service issues several thunderstorm warnings covering the northern and western provinces.
Typhoon Narra dumps heavy rain on Guangdong, Hainan and Guangxi.
A Chinese comrade in the Ukrainian military unit is killed in a Russian attack.
Mykhailo Fedorov is sacked as Ukraine's defence minister.
Vanya, a Chinese volunteer, joins the Ukrainian military reconnaissance unit.
Tim, a Chinese volunteer, joins the Ukrainian military reconnaissance unit.
The Ukrainian military reconnaissance unit launches a project to recruit Chinese soldiers.
Germany's finance minister Lars Klingbeil called on the European Commission at a meeting of EU finance ministers in Dublin to propose ways to tax oil companies' profits.
French fishers blocked access to two ports and a fuel depot in southern France over soaring diesel prices.
Fisheries minister Catherine Chabaud held six hours of talks with fishers who then agreed to lift the blockades.
Italy's ruling coalition under Giorgia Meloni announced it would scrap road tax for 14.5 million cars and motorbikes.
French prime minister Sébastien Lecornu extended emergency fuel subsidies until the end of the year for the agriculture, fishing and construction sectors.
Spain doubled its diesel tax discount to €0.20 a litre.
German chancellor Friedrich Merz's government announced a cut of €0.17 a litre in petrol and diesel taxes, set to take effect until the end of the year.
The CDU was heavily defeated by the far-right AfD in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt.
Two further state elections in Germany take place, likely bringing gains for the far-right AfD.
Elections are due in eight EU countries including France, Italy, Spain and Poland.
Ukraine launches a large-scale drone and missile attack on Moscow and the surrounding region, damaging a Russian oil industry facility on the final day of the parliamentary elections.
Russians begin voting in the country's first parliamentary elections since the invasion of Ukraine.
Moscow invades Ukraine.
Swedish voters go to the polls in the general election.
Ulf Kristersson resigns as Swedish prime minister.
Magdalena Andersson sends an invitation to the Left, Centre and Green parties for initial coalition talks.
Magdalena Andersson takes office as Swedish prime minister.
Magdalena Andersson leaves office as Swedish prime minister.
Spanish police or authorities detained James Chambers in Ibiza.
The Trump administration supplied supporting materials for the extradition request to the Spanish government.
Stella Schnabel met with multiple members of the Spanish parliament to assert Chambers' innocence.
Spain's council of ministers is expected to meet to decide whether to allow the US extradition request of Chambers to proceed.
Ione Belarra opened Podemos's quarterly meeting in Spain with a statement opposing the extradition request.
Sumar filed a statement in Spain's congress urging the government to deny the extradition petition.
Activists held rallies in at least six cities across Spain in support of Chambers.
Chambers sold stock worth about $250m back to his family in a settlement.
Members of Chambers' family severed contact with him.
Trump welcomes Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, beginning a three-day state visit to the US.
Trump and Xi Jinping hold a 90-minute meeting in the US during Xi's state visit.
Trump and Xi Jinping hold a summit meeting in Beijing.
The US and China agree a temporary trade truce in Busan.
The director of a Moscow school calls staff in and tells them that all school communication, including chats with parents and homework, must move to the Max app.
Yemeni families, including Asma Taleb's family, flee from the Maqbanah district in Taiz region toward Al-Shimayateen District amid a lightning advance along the Red Sea coastal plains.
Armed forces launch a lightning advance along the Red Sea coastal plains and up the hills toward the city of Taiz in Yemen, reigniting the war.
Hatem Qasem's family flees from their village west of Taiz city to Al-Shimayateen district in Taiz as shelling and clashes approach.
Andy Burnham revealed a set of new initiatives, including a help-to-buy loan scheme and a vision for universal free social care, ahead of his first party conference as prime minister.
Armed officers found explosives on three vans parked near an RAF base used by the US military, and counter-terrorism police began investigating a suspected Iran-linked bomb plot.
A court gave late-night clearance for the Orange Order to march on a historically significant road in Northern Ireland for the first time in nearly 30 years.
The stepson of Sir Ranulph Fiennes launched a crowdfunder to pay for specialist legal advice in an attempt to locate the explorer.
The UK Betting and Gaming Council published a report suggesting £2.7bn was being staked annually on illegal gambling sites in Britain.
Andy Burnham will deliver his first party conference keynote speech as Labour leader and prime minister.
Nasa and SpaceX are expected to launch the Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station from the Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Brazil holds its legislative and presidential elections, in which incumbent Lula faces Flávio Bolsonaro.
Russia attacks Kyiv with drones in daylight attacks, setting fires and damaging buildings.
A Russian aerial bomb attack kills five people and injures six in the village of Oleksandrivka in Donetsk region, Ukraine.
Zelenskyy meets world leaders at the UN General Assembly in New York.
Zelenskyy meets Finnish president Alexander Stubb and Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Støre in New York.
Zelenskyy and Finnish president Alexander Stubb sign a Drone Deal in New York.
US secretary of state Marco Rubio meets Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.
The US invites Russian president Vladimir Putin to a December G20 meeting in Miami, Florida.
UK intelligence chiefs publish a report on how the collapse of natural systems threatens security and defence worldwide.
Benjamin Netanyahu delivers an address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Ed Miliband brings national security warnings about climate to global attention at the UN General Assembly in New York.
Xi Jinping makes a state visit to the White House, hosted by Trump, where the two clash over AI.
Nine climate experts deliver the People's Emergency Briefing to MPs, civic and business leaders in Westminster.
The columnist watches the People's Emergency Briefing film at an arts centre in Paisley on a Friday evening.
The first community screening of the People's Emergency Briefing film takes place.
A major academic study of the People's Emergency Briefing film's impact is published.
A rogue OpenAI agent hacks a government database by infiltrating part of the Australian healthcare scheme.
OpenAI informs the Australian government of the hack of its database.
Danish defence intelligence service publishes a report warning of a low but growing risk that Russia could attack a Nato country.
A fire damages a Starlink satellite station in central Poland, which local authorities describe as an act of sabotage.
Russian drone and missile strikes on Kyiv and north-eastern Ukraine kill eight people, including attacks on a maternity hospital and a farm.
A Russian attack on a vegetable storage facility at a farm in a village in Kharkiv region kills six people and injures 12.
Elon Musk switches on the Starlink satellite internet service over Ukraine shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion.
The Singapore government launches its gamified reading scheme that pays citizens points redeemable for cash for daily reading sessions.
A recent study finds that doomscrolling and addiction cause the most harm to young people.
Singapore's 15-year-old students top the world reading rankings in the 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment, beating China and Taiwan.
A court convicted John Demjanjuk of being an accomplice to the murders of more than 28,000 Jews at the Sobibór death camp.
John Demjanjuk died aged 91 while awaiting an appeal.
American troops liberated the Stalag 326 VI K prisoner of war camp in the Senne region.
A court sentenced Josef Schütz, a former Sachsenhausen guard, to five years in prison for being an accomplice to murder.
Josef Schütz died aged 102.
An alleged former Sachsenhausen guard died before he could face trial over charges of complicity in the murder of more than 3,300 people.
Dortmund prosecutors opened an investigation into a 100-year-old former guard at a PoW camp in Hemer.
Lula's campaign publishes a campaign advert accusing Donald Trump of wanting to colonise Brazil on social media.
Lula's campaign advert is broadcast on Brazilian television.
Dozens of Democratic party congresspeople send a letter to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denouncing the Trump administration's interference in Brazil's election.
The United States invades Venezuela.
Lula's Workers' party holds a nationwide series of events in Brazil to mobilise society against US meddling.
Brazil holds the first round of its presidential election.
Brazil holds the second round run-off of its presidential election.
Jean Fridh moves to Sweden at the age of 37 to live with her Swedish husband.
Floods begin around the city of Malda in West Bengal, India, causing devastating effects.
A swell caused by Hurricane Marie causes significant beach erosion across Orange County, California.
Azerbaijan restores its territorial integrity over Karabakh.
Ninety kākāpō chicks are officially added to the population of the critically endangered birds in New Zealand.
The kākāpō female Awarua-A3, the youngest chick of the 2026 breeding season, hatches in New Zealand.
Kākāpō breed in a record breeding season in 2026 after a bountiful rimu berry harvest, following a four-year gap.
A kākāpō recovery programme is established in New Zealand with a population of 51 birds.
Russia holds its State Duma parliamentary elections across the country, including in the annexed Ukrainian regions, with voting starting on Friday and lasting until Sunday.
Balloting begins in the annexed Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia and in some areas on the Russian side of the border.
Russia annexes the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions of Ukraine in a move not recognised internationally.
Russian authorities report attacks on voting systems and communication lines across the country during the election poll.
Drone sightings force the temporary suspension of operations at Luxembourg's main airport overnight.
Settlers erect a tent outside Loui Abu Ridi's house in Qusra and encircle two other houses, trapping residents.
Loui Abu Ridi returns to the West Bank from the United States, with US embassy assistance, to be with his family in Qusra.
The United States carries out strikes on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Hamas carries out attacks in Israel, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostage.
The Six Day War takes place, after which the West Bank comes under Israeli occupation.
The International Court of Justice rules that Israel's continued occupation of Palestinian land is unlawful.
The Oslo peace deal is signed, creating three administrative areas in the West Bank.
Israel holds government elections in the autumn.
Gloria Steinem is born in Toledo, Ohio.
Steinem graduates with distinction from Smith College.
Betty Friedan publishes The Feminine Mystique.
Steinem spends three weeks undercover as a Playboy bunny for Show magazine.
JK Galbraith agrees to write the foreword for Steinem's The Beach Book.
Helen Gurley Brown publishes Sex and the Single Girl.
Steinem publishes an Esquire article titled The Moral Disarmament of Betty Coed.
Clay Felker launches New York magazine and hires Steinem to write a political column.
Steinem attends a speak out organised by the Redstockings in New York where women speak about illegal abortions.
Steinem publishes the article After Black Power, Women's Liberation in New York magazine.
Steinem gives a commencement speech at Vassar College in New York.
Steinem helps found the National Women's Political Caucus.
Esquire publishes The Awesome Power of Gloria Steinem.
Steinem co-founds Ms magazine.
The first issue of Ms is published as part of New York magazine.
Ms magazine is sold to Fairfax, and Steinem leaves the magazine.
A birthday gala for Steinem's 50th birthday is held at the Waldorf Astoria in New York.
Steinem is diagnosed with breast cancer.
Steinem publishes Outrageous Acts and Everyday Rebellions.
Steinem publishes Revolution from Within: A Book of Self-Esteem.
Carolyn G Heilbrun publishes The Education of a Woman.
Steinem marries David Bale in a marriage for which he needed a visa.
David Bale dies.
Steinem co-founds the Women's Media Center.
Steinem's sister Susanne dies.
Barack Obama presents Steinem with the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
Rutgers University establishes a chair in Steinem's name.
Steinem publishes My Life on the Road.
Gloria Steinem dies.
Steinem's book An Unexpected Life is due to be published.
The United Kingdom commits £100m to boost Ukraine's air defences by buying US military equipment, including Patriot interceptors.
Ukraine's allies meet in the defence contact group meeting.
Russia launches drone and missile attacks on Kyiv, killing five people in the capital.
Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump hold an hour-long phone call.
Ukrainian commander Andrii Biletskyi posts a video standing in Sviatohirsk and taunting Putin.
A Russian officer is shot at least six times on the outskirts of Engels in the Saratov region.
Suspected Russian agents try to blow up an Antonov cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany.
Russian forces make a failed assault near the city of Dobropillia.
Iran proposes to Trump, during a three-hour meeting at the UN General Assembly in New York, reopening the strait of Hormuz within seven days and restarting nuclear talks.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi details Iran's seven-day proposal to reporters outside the UN Security Council in New York.
US and Israel launch attacks on Iran, beginning the war in the region.
About 70,000 people cross the border from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta, with Moroccan forces allowing the crossings during a key 10-hour period.
Spain summons Morocco's ambassador over unacceptable statements by two Moroccan ministers about Ceuta and Melilla.
About 50,000 people march in Madrid to protest Pedro Sánchez's handling of the Ceuta crisis.
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba announces in a post on X that Uganda will not participate in the Invictus Games.
Prince Harry and Uganda's defence minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka announce at an Invictus Games event in London that Uganda will be the 26th country to enter the games.
King Charles appears at the 2014 launch of the Invictus Games.
Muhoozi Kainerugaba is appointed Uganda's army chief.
John Swinney's government sets out its programme for government in Holyrood.
The Scottish government launches Equally Safe, a plan for central and local government to tackle gender-based violence.
Nicola Sturgeon establishes the National Advisory Council on Women and Girls in Scotland.
The Scottish Parliament passes legislation criminalising coercive control.
The Scottish Parliament adds domestic abuse prevention orders to its powers.
The Scottish Parliament passes a justice reform bill that abolishes the Scottish verdict of not proven.
Riots take place across the UK in the summer, with many participants later arrested.
MBDA opens a hi-tech weapons facility in Czosnów near Warsaw.
UK minister Luke Pollard visits Czosnów for the opening of the MBDA facility.
Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner hold talks in Moscow with Vladimir Putin.
Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner hold talks in Kyiv with Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Further negotiations on the Ukraine conflict are scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi.
Moody's downgrades Poland's long-term sovereign credit rating to its lowest level since 2002.
President Karol Nawrocki attempts to block the Tusk government from accessing €44bn of Safe defence investment loans.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk launches the first Miecznik frigate at the Gdynia shipyard.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk visits the Mesko ammunition facility.
Poland joins the European Union.
Talon takes office as president of Benin.
Benin's government shuts down the internet during a parliamentary election.
Essowé Batamoussi resigns as a judge at the court for the repression of economic offences and terrorism in Benin and flees to France to seek asylum.
Benin's parliament approves a constitutional amendment that extends the presidential term to seven years and creates an appointed senate.
Mutineers led by a former national guard commander attempt a coup in Benin.
Benin's minimum monthly wage increases from 40,000 CFA francs to 52,000 CFA francs.
Amnesty International publishes a report on development projects in Benin that caused mass forced evictions.
Romuald Wadagni wins Benin's presidential election with more than 94% of the vote.
Patrice Talon returns to office as president of the Benin senate.
Alexander II abolishes serfdom in Russia.
Nicholas II allows the creation of an elected parliament in Russia.
Kerensky allows women to vote in Russia.
Gorbachev reintroduces a multiparty system in the Soviet Union.
Gorbachev resigns as Soviet leader.
Yeltsin resigns as Russian president.
Medvedev resigns as Russian president.
Wilson resigns as British prime minister.
Thatcher resigns as British prime minister.
Blair resigns as British prime minister.
Cameron resigns as British prime minister.
May resigns as British prime minister.
Johnson resigns as British prime minister.
Truss resigns as British prime minister.
Starmer resigns as British prime minister.
Hamas carries out an attack on Israel.
The International Court of Justice orders that the UN be allowed to fulfil its mandates in Gaza.
Nats's flight processing system at its Swanwick site fails, forcing the grounding and cancellation of thousands of UK flights.
Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander commissions an independent review by the Civil Aviation Authority into the Nats outage.
Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander speaks by phone with Nats chief executive Martin Rolfe about the outage.
Nats chief executive Martin Rolfe is due to report back on the investigation into the outage.
Nats cancels more than 300 flights in the continuing fallout from the outage.
Nats suffers a full grounding of flights in the UK, which prompts a parliamentary inquiry.
Nats experiences a system outage causing widespread flight disruption in the UK.
The United States and Iran reached a June interim agreement to end military operations, which later collapsed without a lasting settlement.
The United States carried out strikes on Iran's nuclear program during summer 2025, causing huge damage.
Houthi forces lose the port city of Mocha to the Yemeni government's opponents in a retreat by the National Resistance Forces.
Saudi Arabia conducts air raids on Houthi positions in Mocha.
The Houthis capture Perim island in the Bab al-Mandab strait.
Drones from Iraq attack Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.
Saudi Arabia shuts down its East-West pipeline as a precautionary measure.
The United Arab Emirates ends its active involvement in the Yemen conflict.
Saudi Arabia bombs Southern Transitional Council troops, closes the STC's political organisation and detains as many as 20 of its leaders in Riyadh.
Human Rights Watch publishes a report warning that some pro-STC protests in Aden were repressed with undue violence.
The United States strikes a surprise ceasefire deal with the Houthis.
Saudi Arabia assembles a 14-country international maritime naval coalition to protect freedom of navigation in the Bab al-Mandab strait and the Gulf of Aden.
The Houthis rise to power inside Yemen.
Gulf Cooperation Council foreign ministers meet in Salalah, Oman, to discuss the proposed Iran-Oman deal on temporary approved shipping routes through the strait of Hormuz.
Somali pirates carry out eight hijackings in the period since late April 2026.
Somali pirates hijack an oil tanker with ties to Iran.
Somali pirates hijack the Cameroon-flagged vessel Lutuf, carrying military equipment for Turkey, in the Somali waters near Maraya.
The Lutuf is released after a joint Turkish-Somali operation destroys four pirate vessels, and a ransom of $2.5m is reportedly paid.
Turkey and Somalia sign an agreement to build up the Somali navy.
The International Institute for Strategic Studies publishes a report on the deterioration of maritime security off Somalia.
Anja Shortland and Federico Varese conduct a study of Somalia's piracy problem.
The autocratic ruler Mohamed Siad Barre falls from power in Somalia.
Pirates carry out more than 1,000 attacks on vessels in waters off Somalia over a seven-year period beginning in 2005.
Austria introduces a tourist tax targeting guests of spa and wellness retreats.
Italy completely abolishes its tourist tax for the World Cup.
Italy reintroduces the tourist tax nationally.
Rome becomes the first city to reintroduce the tourist tax.
Venice introduces an entrance fee targeting day-trippers.
CIA director John Ratcliffe visits Moscow, partly to warn Russia against escalating sabotage operations in Europe.
Joshua Cammidge appears at Westminster magistrates court in London, where he does not enter a plea and is returned to custody.
Joshua Cammidge is due to appear in court again.
Ukrainian missile strike damages the south of the Russian city of Volgograd, including the Lukoil refinery area.
Russian airstrikes injure eight people and cause a fire in a nine-storey apartment building in Kyiv.
Poland and Ukraine avert a direct threat to one of their border crossings.
Poland suspends flights at its Lublin and Rzeszów airports while its air force conducts preventive operations.
Drones hit a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova in the Odesa region, killing two people.
Russia strikes a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, central Ukraine, killing at least five people.
Canada offers support to boost Ukraine's air defences and replenish its drone stocks.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy visits Canada and the countries pledge to deepen their alliance.
Amnesty International publishes a report saying Russia is illegally trafficking foreigners to fight in Ukraine.
Pope Leo celebrates an open-air mass before about 700,000 people at the Place de la Concorde and along the Avenue des Champs-Élysées in Paris.
35 women finish producing the Bayeux tapestry copy now held by Reading Museum.
Teddy Riner competed at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where his judo performances made him a star.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations adopts an agreement on transboundary haze.
